on premise setups with a lot of companies and tables and containing huge amounts of data and that was the project that we now completed so before presenting the results to you I would like to briefly describe how the replication engine works and highlight the parts of the

replication process that have been improved and then we'll talk about each of the areas in more details as you probably know uh we use Asia data Factory pipelines to copy the data from a source database to the destination when a migration run is triggered the replication pipelines

gets executed and it instructs special compute Services called integration run times to access the data in both the source and the destination databases The Source can be either an un Prem SQL server or an Asia SQL database and the destination is always an Asia SQL of a business

Central tenant so first of all we made quite a lot of improvements uh to the replication pipelines so now they can support larger Cloud migrations and also can migrate wider range of data types during the execution the replication
pipelines use Asia blob storage as a temporary staging unfortunately blob storage introduces its own limitations and and we applied some optimizations to minimize
them the data replication itself is done by two distinct processes the large tables are copied table to table by dedicated copy activities this process has been

optimized the smaller tables are going through the process called B copy during B copy the stored procedures in the on Prem SQL database collect buls of data from many smaller tables serialize and compress each bulk and then split it into records in a special table

then only this table is copied to the cloud where the stored procedures in the tenant database apply the opposite data transformation combine the records together decompress deserialize and push the data into the corresponding tables this process can be repeated for many buls until all data is replicated

and it is very efficient for copying thousands of tables faster but at the same time it's very demanding on the SQL Server compute and input output capabilities and here we made some improvements as well finally it was mentioning that we use SQL change tracking to identify the changes

made to the UN premis data between the replication runs and copy only these incremental changes if it is possible this part has also been improved allowing us to recognize more situations where the Delta syn is possible and reducing the overall migration
time most of these improvements affect migrations from both on premise SQL silver and Asia SQL but there are some that make a huge difference specifically for Asia SQL
sources so let's look at this improvements in more details and see how you can benefit from them in your future

migrations looking at the replication pipelines we changed the way the replication method data has been passed between the source and the destination instead of using the data Factory activities input and output parameters we now copy the metadata through a database table and this allowed

us to bypass the 4 meab um data Factory limitation on the activities input and output so it has become possible to replicate an unlimited number of tables in a single migration run and we remove the limitation on the number of companies being replicated of course it's important to remember that business Central

supports not more than 300 companies in single environment but now all these companies can be replicated in one single run if you have a powerful on premise SQL Server um apart from this we also removed the calculation on the on premise database size from the replication

runs uh this calculation is done once during the cloud migration setup and not repeating it during replication can save between 15 and 45 minutes for large Source databases and reduce the probability of timeouts and finally we expanded the replication pipelines with

the activity scoping SQL sequences specific for business Central so now the AL number sequences data type is supported by Cloud migration and the numbering can continue in the BC tenant after migration instead of being

reset so for table totable copy let's look at the optimizations here table totable copy is used for large tables uh however we reduce the threshold now the replication engine picks uh would pick a table for table totable copy

if the data size to be migrated exceeds 250 megabyte and it used to be 500 megabyte before so this means that more tables are going through table totable copy now and the replication status is updated faster for these

tables uh also tables with a lot of data tend to have many indexes defined when the data is copied all these indexes have to to be updated on every insert now we disable the indexes in the Target table before copying its data and rebuild the indexes after the data is replicated
and our test measurement show 8 to 22% performance benefit for the new process comparing to the old way of inserting the data with all indexes

enabled because both the cleanup of the target table and the data copy are now happening with no active indexes uh the replication runs are much faster and this allowed to prevent the timeouts for the large tables replication for the bul copy of the smaller tables

in addition to the reduced threshold we also reduce the bulk size so this resulted in higher numbers of smaller bulks and smaller bulks are easier for the SQL s to serialize and compress so the timeouts occurrences become rare also
they may still happen for the extremely weak or busy SQL service in fact this gave a significant performance benefit on our not very powerful test servers the whole process of B copy became 60 to 80%

faster the replication status is also updated more frequently if the buls are smaller we also made the diagnostic runs respect the bulk size before they tried to process all data in single huge bulk and that often led to timeouts and out of memory exceptions
now diagnostic runs utilize the same smaller buls as the normal replication runs they don't time out and you can safely use them to quickly test the future
replication finally optimizations for the Delta sync of the incremental changes which are related to our usage of SQL change

tracking so if the changes between two change tracking versions can be reliably collected the replication engine performs a fast Delta sync otherwise the whole table has to be cleaned up and replicated again so we forced a longer change track and retention period that allowed the change tracking versions to

stay valid longer and that increases the probability of the fast Delta sychronization for the repeated replication runs and we changed the code to use change tracking in wider range of the situations for example Delta sync is now possible also for the databases that first enable

change tracking specifically for cloud migration and now Delta sinks are happening more often reducing the overall migration time so all the improvements mentioned earlier are applied to both SQL server and Asia SQL sources however if uh Asia SQL

is used a source it is possible to link the source and the destination Asia SQL databases directly without the requirement of the serialized staging in a asure blob storage and removing staging allow it to make the replication faster so now we don't have to serialize

and deserialize the data and it has become possible to replicate the fields of SQL variant type also the errors caused by The Blob infrastructure are going away for example trying to copy a record with large value in a single field like image sometimes fails in the staging blop with a message

that the specified road delimit is incorrect so this won't happen for the migration from Asia SQL anymore so in general with all these changes Asia SQL becomes a more powerful and better performing alternative to the SQL Server as a source for cloud migration so if you have plans for some

high volume migrations you might consider deploying on premise database to an Asia SQL first and if you want to migrate SQL variant fields or Fields with large images then Asia SQL as a source would be the only possibility so the process of deploying an Asia to Asia SQL

is it can be quite fast if you have uh the right service tier in your as SQL database it is also well described in the the SQL online help how fast it can be depends on the service tier that you have to choose for your SQL for the for your Asia SQL database

and our recommendation here is to prioritize its compute and input output capabilities of course Asia SQL is not for free and you would probably have to balance the cost and the benefit but the more powerful service tier you get the faster and smoother your Cloud migrations will be and with that
